setter.name: Kim Forbes-Sobers
setter.evidence: Rep: 'So, Matthew, I've spoke to Kim. You had a call with Kim. few days ago, yeah?' Prospect: 'Yeah.' The prospect independently confirms it later — 'when I talked to Kim yesterday or the day before'. Setter notes were used mid-call: 'because Kim told me you work as a director in a security company that's correct'. Note the title carries no KFS suffix, so the code is recovered from content only.

prospect.name: Matthew
prospect.location: Canada, Eastern time zone; native French speaker and prices in Canadian dollars
prospect.occupation: Director at a security company — management position, client-facing, presents to rooms, travels for work, works from home and on the road, describes 18-hour days
prospect.family_status: Married or long-term partner ('my wife and my kids'); two daughters aged five and seven
prospect.training_background: Fit and athletic until about 25 — trained three to four times a week from age 18, ran, lifted, boxed. Currently doing nothing. Has a treadmill and once completed three unbroken months of 10,000 steps a day ending February this year. Recently started a Jiu Jitsu/Krav Maga style course but stopped two weeks ago when his training partner quit.
prospect.medical: No conditions or injuries disclosed — and none were asked about. He volunteered unprompted that he has a testosterone test booked for a few weeks' time: 'I'm getting a test done in a couple weeks for my testosterone.' Self-reports roughly 40 lb of excess fat, afternoon energy crashes, and six to seven hours of sleep with sub-five-minute sleep onset.

signals: Explicit former self to recover — fit at 18, trained three to four times a week, boxed; lost it from about 25 when the kids and the workload arrived
Visible regret and self-judgement: 'now I'm at my worst', 'it's weird that I still do this... I know it's so bad', 'I have a good 40 pounds too much of pure fat'
Frames every other area of life as already won — 'Now I'm successful at work. I feel like I'm successful in life, what I own, what I have... It's just more the physical'
Knowledge is not the gap and he says so — 'I know more than the standard person about like what to eat, how to eat, and how to work out. I just don't apply it'
Not the_optimizer: he is not asking for good-to-great, he is asking to get back what he had

goals.text: Be in shape for his two daughters and be a good example for them
Get the executive presence back — his new boss is fit and he presents in front of people; 'having that image is a bit better'
Stop the burnt-out afternoon crash that costs him two or three productive hours a day
Lose roughly 40 lb of body fat
Have external structure and accountability rather than another self-run attempt
Training he can take on the road — 'I can just put them in the car and bring them with me'

pains.text: Knows exactly what to do and does not do it — 'I know what to do, and I know one day I'll get there. I just have to, like, do the switch'
No structure at all around training or food — 'now I'm like free for all. Like, no limits'
Diet is at its worst — random McDonald's, two chocolate bars back to back, eating out constantly with clients
Afternoon energy collapse — 'I could waste a good two, three hours of my day trying to actually survive... I'm not being productive as I should be'
Cannot commit to a fixed weekly slot — out of office, travelling, 'I can't have a fixed date every Tuesday night'
Stress-eating tied to deadlines and workload, which the rep named and he confirmed
Attempts collapse when the external prop is removed — the 10,000-step streak ended the week he got back from Mexico, the Krav Maga stopped when his partner quit
Carries it privately — 'it's something I haven't really necessarily told people about, people that are close'

objections.raw_quote: This is where the silence becomes, I'm comparing with my, I'll be honest, I'm comparing with my colleague's personal trainer, which he's at 600 a month. And it's not necessarily the same as Trevor, but that's my comparison of pricing.
objections.rep_response: Did not address the price gap. Pivoted to modality specialisation — that CrossFit and most of the space teach kettlebells badly, and Trevor's expertise is kettlebells, steel maces and calisthenics. Asked the prospect to 'take that in consideration'.

objections.raw_quote: I understand the pricing. I'm not surprised. I'm a bit surprised it's a bit steeper than I thought it was.
objections.rep_response: Later restated by the prospect as 'It's pretty much double what I thought it would have been'. The rep responded by inventing a one-month $1,200 entry rather than isolating the objection or running the financial picture.

objections.raw_quote: It's weird to say. I don't really know him. I've seen a couple videos.
objections.rep_response: Cited the guarantee and argued that no amount of testimonial substitutes for starting — 'You can read all the testimonials, see your friend doing it, but until you actually start doing this and seeing yourself, you cannot say anything about whether it's going to work or not.'

objections.raw_quote: Interesting. I'd like to still take time to think about it, though.
objections.rep_response: Named the pattern — 'you told me in the beginning that you've been putting this off time and time again. And this is happening again, man. And you know it. What's coming up? Be honest, be frank.' — then, after the prospect held, offered a Friday follow-up: 'I don't want to force you to anything. Let's do this. Let's follow up on Friday.'

objections.raw_quote: I don't know if it would be better having someone more local and someone that I see that there's results, like, I have my colleague that's 400 pounds down to, like, 185, 190
objections.rep_response: Not addressed. The rep moved to the fitness-is-unknowable-until-you-start argument and the guarantee, then to the $1,200 trial. The local-versus-remote preference was never engaged.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Improvised live after the prospect hesitated: 'Check out Trevor for a month for 1200. He will map out the whole program for you... If you don't like it after one month, you will say that, and okay, that's fine. We'll shake hands... However, when you're going to like it... you can move for another five months. And you just top that up with the remaining price.' The remaining amount, the total under this route, and what happens to the $1,200 if he stops at one month were never stated. A Canadian-dollar figure was also improvised — the rep said 'I think it's going to be 7, 7-ish' and the number '8, 5' appears immediately after in the transcript.
offer.guarantee_mentioned: Stated twice. First: 'there's a guarantee on that also in writing.' Then in terms: 'he gives you a real guarantee on that, that if you want to... achieve the goals, which are adding more, adding at least eight kilos to your baseline kettlebell moves. He will work for you, work with you until you actually do that. And he will work with you for free.'

evidence: No payment, no link, no verbal agreement to proceed on either the $6,000 or the $1,200 route

Prospect held firm across three separate pushes: 'I'd like to still take time to think about it', 'I want to take a bit of time, I want to think about it, and I could get back to you by the end of the week', 'that's something I have a rule. I've never just go in without taking a night's sleep'
Follow-up booked and accepted live — Friday 2pm Eastern; the prospect confirmed 'I got the invitation. I accepted it'
Prospect committed to deciding: 'I'll all the information for this Friday and I'll be able to give a decision Friday'

Counter-evidence toward a positive read: he gave a genuine verbal yes to the commitment question ('the answer is yes. I'm no choice'), volunteered 'I'm for sure doing something. I have to do something. It's not necessarily like an option', and proposed the follow-up himself — 'I'm even down if you want to schedule another meeting... That'd be my accountability'
Counter-evidence toward a negative read: he is going to call the competing local trainer first — 'I'm going to give them a call, see what's up, and if it doesn't work well, I'll come back'
outcome.next_step: Follow-up Zoom on Friday at 2pm Eastern, invite sent and accepted on the call. Rep committed to emailing additional information and videos the next day. Prospect will speak to his colleague and contact the colleague's local trainer in the meantime.

notable.note: Price was cut to a $1,200 one-month entry on hesitation alone, and roughly three minutes later the prospect stated plainly that price was never the blocker: 'even if you're like at $2,000 for six months, I still would have been like, okay, let me get my second opinion on this.' The discount bought nothing because the real objection — an unknown remote provider versus a local trainer with a visible 200 lb result on a colleague at $600 a month — was surfaced and then never worked. Separately, this is a self-described 40-lb-overweight, currently untraining prospect who was taken through the full pillar presentation and priced without a single injury, pain, limitation or health-condition question being asked. The discovery on this call was otherwise the strongest in the batch: root cause was genuinely excavated and a real commitment yes was obtained before the number.

quality.notes: Short turns are frequently attributed to the wrong speaker and several long passages run under one label while containing both voices — the block at 00:11:42-00:14:00 labelled Matthew contains the rep's stress-eating question and the director-at-a-security-company confirmation, and the segment at 00:25:35 attributes the rep's 'do you feel like this approach would actually work for you?' to the prospect. Roles assigned from content. The substance of the call is clear despite this; only line attribution is unreliable.
